positions.title: AML/CFT Subject-Matter Expert — Cryptocurrency Financial Crime & Compliance
positions.company: Aras Integrasi Sdn Bhd — ChainSentry Product Division
positions.products: ChainSentry (forensics & E-KYC) with the chain: family — chain:HARVEST (wallet intelligence) and the identity layer
positions.reports_to: Solutions Architect / Product Lead, ChainSentry — dotted line to COO for contractual and commercial matters
positions.direct_reports: None at appointment; owns analyst/contractor support as the design-partner cohort scales
positions.grade: Senior Executive / Assistant Manager (4–8 years relevant experience)
positions.location: Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia (hybrid). **Travel:** ~15–20% — Ho Chi Minh City, Bangkok, Dubai, occasionally Manama, Istanbul, Zürich
positions.employment_type: Full-time, permanent; three-month probation with structured objectives (Section 9)
positions.remuneration: Competitive band aligned to Malaysian financial-crime market norms (band confirmed by COO before posting); medical, travel allowance, funded CAMS/ICA renewal, professional-body membership

3.1 Compliance-by-design for pilots and: Draft, negotiate and administer the design-partner agreement suite: pilot term sheets, written-reference and quotation clauses, sanitised labelled-case contribution terms, and the data-rights clause that treats a pilot's labelled dispositions as paid consideration.
Maintain the pilot compliance matrix — legal basis, cross-border data categories, hosting location, retention and destruction/return obligations — for every active pilot.

Pre-empt jurisdiction blockers as a habit: Malaysian PDPA and AMLA 2001 handling for law-enforcement and reporting-institution data; Swiss banking-secrecy treatment for FIU-type submissions; UAE federal and emirate-level rules across VARA and SCA regimes; Vietnamese and Egyptian pilot-documentation obligations.
Run pre-launch compliance reviews with engineering and close-out reviews that certify what corpus material may lawfully return to the shared corpus, in what sanitised form, under which clause.
3.2 Crypto AML operations: sanctions and: Own the sanctioned-address and watchlist labelling pipeline end to end: OFAC SDN, EU, UK (OFSI) and UN lists, court-document addresses, ransomware-payment trackers and takedown archives converted into deterministic, versioned, source-cited seed labels.
Define label acceptance criteria and QA machine-generated clusters; nothing enters the production corpus without a provenance chain that survives the question "where did this attribution come from?"
Operate and tune the sanctions-screening engine for corridor clusters and settlement rails — match-type weighting, coin-type validation, false-positive handling, escalation paths.

Stay current on the emerging typologies the corridor produces — bridge-exploit fund dispersal, privacy-coin conversion flows (shielded/transparent transitions), cross-chain hop obscuration, stolen-funds laundering-as-a-service — and convert them into detection and label logic.
3.3 Typology casework and court-grade re: Conduct blockchain tracing casework during pilots: mule-network mapping, scam-centre fund-flow reconstruction, exchange off-ramp identification, mixer and peel-chain handling, cross-chain bridge hops.

Produce tracing reports at brief and court grade (MY, UAE and CH flavours) with methodology statements, evidence and source citations, limitations, reproducibility appendices and a plain-language executive summary an investigator can forward unedited.
Support law-enforcement design partners through their internal processes — investigation-paper support in the Malaysian flavour, jointly agreed cases, within agreed data boundaries.
Build the report-template library from real cases; iterate against actual reader feedback at customer institutions.
3.4 Regulatory, FIU and law-enforcement: Serve as technical-compliance counterpart for Bank Negara Malaysia (Financial Integrity/Payments), Securities Commission Malaysia, VARA, SCA, the UAE FIU, Bahrain's CBB, Turkey's MASAK and SPK, Egypt's FRA and FIU, and Swiss FIU-class bodies.

Author supervisory-grade artefacts: discussion papers, public-consultation responses arguing proportionate surveillance standards, baseline guidance (for example, "AML/CFT expectations for a newly licensed digital-asset exchange").
Prepare and co-present capability briefings to investigator audiences on methodology and recorded public-data output.
Support MENAFATF/FATF-adjacent positioning: Recommendation 15 coverage, Travel Rule obligations and implementation practice across the roster states.
3.5 Commercial, bid and enablement suppo: Act as named AML/CFT SME on RFP/tender responses and supplier due-diligence questionnaires; own the reusable compliance-answers library.
Review prospects' AML policies, travel-rule posture and tooling as the diagnostic hook of "day-one AML" bundles for newly licensed VASPs.
Support pricing conversations on compliance substance — what a proportionate licence covers, what an address-band includes, why seat-based incumbent pricing misaligns for supervised SMBs.
Deliver methodology workshops and investigator training during pilots.
3.6 Internal influence and product feedb: Convert pilot friction into product backlog: data-handling gaps, report-format gaps, audit-log requirements, jurisdiction-specific features.
Hold standing recommend-block authority in corpus and pilot reviews on unlawful data movement — the recommendation is recorded; engineering is required to answer.

success_horizons.outcome: Pilot agreement suite + data-rights annex drafted; jurisdictional legal map covering the seed markets produced with named blockers escalated in writing

100% of signed pilots on the compliance template; sanctions/watchlist labelling pipeline operational with weekly refresh (<48h from list publication); first MY-flavour court-grade report accepted by a design partner

Sanctions screening live for at least two design-partner use cases with documented false-positive handling; first public artefact (consultation response or methodology section) submitted; analyst supervision begun as cohort scales

≥8 design partners on active, compliant pilots with zero unresolved compliance findings; label-provenance QA at 100% of the production corpus; precision/recall methodology published for one corridor; ≥2 customer-named written references enabled (1 government, 1 VASP)

required_common: 4–8 years in AML/CFT, financial-crime compliance or financial-crime investigations, of which at least 2 years hands-on with blockchain/digital-asset crime: typologies, on-chain tracing, exchange risk monitoring, Travel Rule operations.

Perspective earned on the buy side or enforcement side: VASP compliance function, bank AML/CFT or transaction-monitoring unit, FIU analyst, law-enforcement financial-crime analyst, or a forensic/consultancy crypto-investigations practice. Vendor-side pre-sales alone does not satisfy this.

Working fluency in FATF standards as applied to virtual assets (Recommendation 15, Travel Rule/IVMS101), plus demonstrated working knowledge of at least one of: Malaysian AMLA 2001 with BNM/SC digital-asset policy; the UAE federal framework with VARA/SCA rulebooks; Turkish Law No. 7518 with MASAK regulation; Swiss GATA/AMLO and VQF-class SRO practice; Egyptian Law 162/2023 with FRA regulations.

Able to follow USDT-on-TRON through peel chains, peel-and-return patterns, mixer entry and bridge hops using public explorers and clustering tooling without assistance. You do not write production code, but you never need tracing done for you.
Regulatory-grade English prose; writing sample required at shortlist.
Comfortable with law-enforcement-grade material: classification, need-to-know and chain-of-custody as habits, not policies.
CAMS active, or committed within 12 months with employer-supported study.
nice_to_have: Certification: CFCS, ICA, CICAM or equivalent.
Operating experience on incumbent tracing platforms (Chainalysis, TRM Labs, Elliptic) — you will help compete against them honestly, including on import/export compatibility.
Privacy-coin typology depth (Zcash transparent/shielded econometrics, Monero view-key practice) — a deliberate product wedge.
Published AML/CFT or digital-asset policy writing; expert-witness or consultation-submission history.
E-KYC/fraud-assurance awareness (document authentication, deepfake detection, identity assurance levels) — the identity console falls inside this role's advisory perimeter.
Languages: English mandatory (written); Malay strong advantage; Arabic, Turkish, Vietnamese or Russian genuine differentiators.

offer: Genuine ownership: the compliance doctrine of a sovereign blockchain-forensics product is written by this role, not inherited.
Year-one exposure to central banks, FIUs and police financial-crime units across three continents.
Authority matched to accountability — blocking recommendations are recorded and answered, not absorbed.
Funded certification and professional-body participation; publication credit under your own name.
A small team, direct access to leadership, and a stated kill/continue culture: honest bad news is valued over managed optimism.
positions.engagement_terms: Full-time, permanent; KL hybrid; band **INDICATIVE pending COO confirmation before any posting**; probation three months with structured objectives; formal NDA and classification discipline from day one. Alternative engagement modes (senior fractional / advisory retainer) may be discussed for exceptional candidates; the default is employment.
positions.application: Submit CV plus a one-page writing sample responding to: *"What should a newly licensed digital-asset exchange in your jurisdiction be required to have in place on day one for transaction monitoring — and what is proportionate?"* Shortlisted candidates complete a live public-chain tracing exercise and a clause-negotiation conversation with the hiring panel. Applications to **[careers contact — confirm before posting]**.

positions.title: Blockchain Developer (Junior / Middle) — Forensics & Data Platform
positions.company: Aras Integrasi Sdn Bhd — ChainSentry Product Division
positions.reports_to: Solutions Architect / Product Lead, ChainSentry — engineering mentoring from the senior engineering bench
positions.grade: Two bands hire against this single posting — Junior (0–2 years) and Middle (2–4 years)
positions.employment_type: Full-time, permanent; three-month probation with structured objectives
positions.remuneration: Band aligned to the Malaysian engineering market by level (INDICATIVE pending COO confirmation before posting); medical coverage; hardware and learning budget

3.1 On-chain data engineering: Build and maintain ingestion services that acquire, parse, normalise and index on-chain data across multiple networks (Bitcoin-family, Ethereum/EVM, TRON, Solana), from raw RPC through to storage.
Implement and extend address-codec validation per chain — Base58Check, Bech32/Bech32m, EIP-55 checksums — treating validation as a gate, not a suggestion.
Work with the crawler fleet's output: idempotent upserts, deduplication across sources, schema evolution without losing provenance columns.
3.2 Enrichment and intelligence pipeline: Extend the enrichment engines: contract-vs-EOA classification via `eth_getCode`, token-metadata resolution, explorer reconciliation, sanctions-list joins.
Build new collection veins as coverage expands (including privacy-coin transparent-address handling and cross-chain bridge event mapping).
Keep false-positive rates measurable: every heuristic gets a precision story, and you will instrument it.
3.3 Forensics product features: Ship investigator-facing features in the Next.js/TypeScript app: cluster-graph exploration, trace timelines, case-pack export, watchlist views.
Own the graph layer pragmatically — layout performance on large clusters, sensible edge semantics, clean interaction for non-technical examiners.
3.4 Sanctions and compliance engineering: Harden the sanctions-import path: OFAC SDN (XML/JSON/CSV), EU/UK/UN list variants, deterministic address extraction, versioned and dated imports.
Tune matching behaviour with the AML/CFT SME: exact vs fuzzy matching thresholds, coin-type validation, scoring weights — with documented, reversible changes.
3.5 Surfaces and integrations: Maintain and extend the MCP tool layer so agentic clients can consume ChainSentry capabilities safely (authentication, scoping, tool contracts).
Build and maintain internal APIs consumed by the app, the pipelines, and partner integrations.
3.6 Quality, security and operations: Practise the team's discipline: checksum-validated ingestion, secret-free commits, dependency review, migration discipline on PostgreSQL, containerised deploys to Linux hosts.
Take part in deployment and incident triage for owned systems — you ship it, you keep it alive.

success_horizons.outcome: At least one shipped ingestion/validation change in production with tests; can walk through the codec stack (Base58Check vs Bech32m vs EIP-55) unaided; first PR merged into the crawler or app codebase
Owns one ingestion vein end to end (source, validation, storage, monitoring); one enrichment heuristic instrumented with a measurable precision figure; onboarding doc for that vein exists

Delivers a forensics app feature through to production (Middle) or a significant component of one (Junior); sanctions-import path handles at least two list variants deterministically; participates in deploy rotations

Recognisable owner of a subsystem the AML/CFT SME trusts for casework evidence; MCP/tooling contributions shipped; zero data-provenance regressions attributable to owned code; able to brief a non-technical reviewer on the corpus's data journey

required_common: JavaScript/TypeScript and Python are your working languages; SQL (PostgreSQL) is second nature.
Concrete grasp of blockchain fundamentals: transactions, UTXO vs account models, addresses vs keys, confirmations, and why address encodings differ per chain.
Git discipline you do not have to be reminded about; comfort in Linux environments; willingness to carry deploys.
Bias to verification: you would rather measure than assert — checksums, tests, logs.
required_middle: Production experience in at least one of: data-pipeline/backhaul engineering, Web3/on-chain services, or fintech backend systems.
Demonstrable asynchronous-worker and queue patterns; schema-evolution experience on live datasets.
Familiarity with at least one major chain's tooling ecosystem (ethers/viem, bitcoinlib, explorer APIs).
required_junior: A portfolio that proves hands-on work: shipped projects, freelance builds, or substantial open-source/contribution history touching blockchains, scrapers, or data tooling.
The trajectory matters more than the years: evidence you learn fast and finish things.
nice_to_have: Rust or Go alongside the core stack.
Front-end graph experience (Cytoscape, D3, xyflow) or real MCP/tool-API design.
Privacy-coin curiosity (Zcash address model, transparent vs shielded flows) — a deliberate product wedge; you would help build its first vein.
Docker production operations; conversational Mandarin for regional vendor coordination.

offer: Production ownership uncommon at this level: your services run in sovereign deployments where a foreign vendor would be a black box.
Dual craft development: data engineering and forensics product work in one seat.
Direct access to the product lead and the AML/CFT SME; no layers between your code and the investigator who uses it.
Hardware and learning budget; funded attendance at regional security/blockchain community events.
A stated kill/continue culture — measured results and honest bad news beat managed optimism.
positions.engagement_terms: Full-time, permanent; KL hybrid; band **INDICATIVE pending COO confirmation before any posting** (junior and middle bands distinguished by level); probation three months with structured objectives; NDA applies — portions of the work touch law-enforcement-adjacent casework and customer compliance data.
positions.application: Submit CV or portfolio plus a short note on a piece of data tooling you built and what broke first. Shortlisted candidates complete a practical exercise: validate, ingest and enrich a small raw address dataset (codec edge cases included) and walk through your choices in a technical conversation. Applications to **[careers contact — confirm before posting]**.
